description: Representing the Scientific Society (Naukkom) of FFECS at DNU for NASA Space Apps Challenge, our team is building autonomous software to monitor astronaut health during lunar missions (Artemis). Designed for deep-space communication delays, our platform tracks real-time biometrics, predicts physiological risks from radiation, microgravity, and stress, and delivers actionable medical insights. We combine FFECS’s engineering rigor with modern IT for safer lunar exploration.
summary: FPECS is a software system designed to monitor and analyze the health parameters of astronauts during long-duration space missions. The project simulates the collection of astronaut health telemetry, stores the received data in a PostgreSQL database, and provides a desktop interface for monitoring and analyzing health indicators. The system includes separate modules for data simulation, telemetry processing, database management, and visualization. Its goal is to demonstrate how continuous health monitoring and timely detection of abnormal parameters can support astronaut safety and help mission teams make informed decisions during space exploration.
details:
The FPECS project focuses on developing a modular software solution for astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions.

The system consists of several interconnected components. A telemetry simulator generates astronaut health data. A data receiver processes incoming information, while a dispatcher manages telemetry transmission and storage. PostgreSQL is used to maintain historical health records. The analysis component processes the collected data and identifies potentially abnormal health indicators. A desktop graphical interface provides access to telemetry, monitoring information, and system status.

The project is being developed using Rust, with support for Linux and Windows environments. Special attention is given to modular architecture, reliable data storage, and the ability to expand the system in the future.

FPECS demonstrates a possible approach to organizing astronaut health telemetry and supporting mission control through centralized data collection, analysis, and visualization.
